findings.title: Destructuring an empty destinationCalendar array causes TypeError
findings.body: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` can yield `undefined`, and the next line dereferences it unguarded: `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar"`. For any booking with Google Meet as location and no destination calendar (now commonly `[]` or `null`, e.g. handleCancelBooking and the stripe/paypal webhooks pass `[]`), `EventManager.create` throws `Cannot read properties of undefined`, breaking booking creation. Use optional chaining.

findings.title: updateEvent/deleteEvent fallback lookup is always undefined
findings.body: `const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;` — the `find` branch only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so it compares each `cal.externalId` against `undefined` and can never match. The previous code fell back to `event.destinationCalendar.externalId`. Result: when no externalCalendarId is stored on the reference, `calendarId` becomes undefined and the Google update/delete targets the wrong (default) calendar or fails. The same pattern exists in `deleteEvent` (line 317), where it then silently falls back to `primary`.

findings.title: externalId not recorded for destinations without credentialId
findings.body: In the `else` branch (destination without `credentialId`), `createEvent(c, event)` is called without the third `externalId` argument, so `EventResult.externalId` is undefined and the booking reference gets `externalCalendarId: undefined` (line 169 now derives it from `result.externalId` instead of `evt.destinationCalendar.externalId`). Subsequent updates/cancellations then cannot locate the event in the right calendar.

findings.title: Possible duplicate event creation for *_other_calendar destinations
findings.body: After the destination loop, all credentials whose type includes `other_calendar` are unconditionally used to create another event. If a destinationCalendar entry points to one of those credentials (its `credentialId` matches, or its `integration` equals the credential type), the event is created twice for that integration, producing duplicate calendar entries and duplicate booking references.

findings.title: Team destination calendars dropped when evt.destinationCalendar is null
findings.body: `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is a no-op when `destinationCalendar` is `null` (which happens when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar). In a collective event where only the non-organizer hosts have calendars connected, their calendars are silently ignored — exactly the case this PR aims to fix. Initialize to `[]` and push instead.

findings.title: Dynamic booking user select lost `organization.slug`
findings.body: The rewritten `loadUsers` drops `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` from the dynamic (no eventTypeId) user query that the previous code selected. Any downstream code relying on `user.organization?.slug` (e.g. booker/organizer URL construction for org users) will now see it missing for dynamic group bookings.

findings.title: BOOKING_CREATED/BOOKING_REQUESTED webhook assertions not updated for array payload
findings.body: Only the BOOKING_REJECTED expectation was changed to `destinationCalendar: []`. The BOOKING_CREATED (line 119) and BOOKING_REQUESTED (line 373) expectations still assert `destinationCalendar: null`, but `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` is now an array (`[]` or a list). These assertions will fail or, worse, pass accidentally and no longer verify the payload shape.

findings.title: Legacy-reference cancellation path now deletes once per reference per credential
findings.body: The loop over all `_calendar` references combined with the inner `else` branch (iterating every user calendar credential) means for N legacy references with M calendar credentials, M*N delete calls are issued, each using that reference's `uid`/`externalCalendarId` against unrelated credentials. This multiplies API calls and generates spurious 404s compared to the previous single-reference behavior.
